\chapter{Design Analysis}

The design analysis of the electromagnetic brake joint is divided into four hierarchical layers, inculding the WSoI which encompasses the testsing enviornment and the PCMA arm, the NSoI representing the joint, its functional subsystems, and the individual components. The physical development of the joint was iterative, however, the resulting architecture is documented in a logical, top-down fashion instead of a chronological sequence. To describe the system's integration, the analysis is split into three domains which constitute the mechanical design, the electronic design, and the software design. The mechanical design outlines the spatial arrangement and loading paths. The electronic design describes the peripheral circuitry and power interfacing. The software design defines the control logic and the state machine controlling the electromagnetic brake.

\section{Mechanical Design}

Figure~\ref{fig:screenshot001} below, shows the 3D CAD assembly of the electromagnetic brake produced as part of the design analysis after integration and refinement of the individual subsystem concepts.

\begin{figure}[H]
	\centering
	\includegraphics[width=0.7\linewidth]{../../../../../../../../../Downloads/screenshot001}
	\caption{Electromagnetic Brake Assembly}
	\label{fig:screenshot001}
\end{figure}

The top-level system elements are listed in the drawing's materials list and are marked with balloon numbers in Figure~\ref{fig:screenshot001}. The different views and dimensions of the engineering drawing depict the position of physical interfaces with elements external to the NSoI and the spatial constraints for the respective system elements inside the NSoI.

The overall configuration uses an electromagnetic brake mounted coaxially on the joint shaft. In the configuration, the base link and the output link are integrated with the internal actuation and sensing components. The joint is supported by two roller bearings mounted with an inteference fit and secured by shaft collars to prevent axial slipping. The bearing housing is integrated directly into the stationary joint housing. The housing encases the internal mechanisms and is held rigid by the base link. On one of the shaft, the high resolution optical encoder is connected via a rigid coupling. A spacer sits on the side of the encoder shaft to compensate for the discrepancy in diameters of the joint, the encoder, and the rigid coupling\footnote{See Appendix \#\# for calculations regarding the joint shaft  design.}. On the opposite end, the electromagnetic brake assembly interfaces directly with the shaft. The electromagnetic brake consist of solenoids, friction plate, and a brake disc.

This configuration was chosen because it provides a reliable, uniform clamping force that minimises parasitic deflections and preserves the run-out tolerances necessary for the PCMA's spatial accuracy. Addionally, by housing the brake internally, the design is able to achieve the full \SI{90}{\degree} operational articulation sweep.

To maintain structural integrity and positional stability during locking, the electromagnetic brake was sized to deliver a static holding of \SI{7.725}{Nm}, corrsponding to a electromagntive force of \SI{3 550}{N}. The freebody diagrams (FBDs) and design calculations supporting the mechanical operating conditions of the joint under Appendix \#\#.
